record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.original_question: Can near-extremal, higher-dimensional, maximally rotating, charged, or memory-burden-suppressed PBHs remain stable on cosmological timescales after Hawking evaporation would otherwise remove them, and can such relics be detected directly in terrestrial detectors or indirectly through high-energy emission from occasional binary mergers?

evidence.quote: Furthermore, near-extremal PBHs provide an intriguing means of making evaporating PBHs stable on cosmological scales.

Formation is simplest for low mass five-dimensional PBHs that initially act like four-dimensional PBHs, Hawking radiating down to the radius of the extra dimension where their effective temperature is effectively zero, to attain a stable mass [19].

Other scenarios for producing near-extremal PBH include formation of maximally rotating or charged PBH at very early epochs [21], as well as via the quantum gravity phenomenon of so-called memory burden suppression [22]. Detectability is feasible down to scales as small as a few Planck masses for charged PBH relics via terrestrial detectors [23] or equally for high energy particle emission from occasional binary merger events [24].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider primordial black holes (PBHs), i.e. black holes hypothesized to have formed in the early universe from large density perturbations or other mechanisms, with initial masses small enough that standard semiclassical Hawking radiation would cause them to fully evaporate on a timescale shorter than the present age of the universe.

For each of the following classes of PBHs, determine whether they can remain stable, or at least extremely long-lived (with lifetimes exceeding the current age of the universe), as cosmological relics, and determine whether such relics admit feasible direct or indirect observational signatures:

(a) Near-extremal four-dimensional Reissner–Nordström or Kerr–Newman PBHs whose charge or angular momentum is tuned close to the extremal bound, so that the Hawking temperature is parametrically small.

(b) Higher-dimensional PBHs in models with compact extra dimensions of size L: in particular, low-mass five-dimensional PBHs that initially behave as four-dimensional Schwarzschild black holes and Hawking radiate down to a horizon radius comparable to L, where their effective temperature approaches zero and the evaporation stalls.

(c) Maximally rotating PBHs or maximally charged PBHs formed at very early cosmological epochs, so that their initial spin or charge parameter saturates the extremal bound.

(d) PBHs whose evaporation is strongly suppressed by the conjectured quantum-gravitational "memory burden" effect, in which the back-reaction of stored quantum information halts or strongly slows semiclassical Hawking emission once a comparable fraction of the initial mass has been radiated.

For each class, specify the conditions (mass range, charge or spin, extra-dimension size, suppression parameter) under which the resulting object is stable on cosmological timescales. In addition, assess whether such relics—possibly down to mass scales as small as a few Planck masses for charged PBH relics—can be detected either directly in terrestrial detectors sensitive to charged or strongly-interacting massive particle-like objects, or indirectly through high-energy particle emission generated by occasional binary mergers of such relics.
artifact.status_search_result: The viability and detection of near-extremal, higher-dimensional, maximally charged/rotating, and memory-burdened PBH relics are the subject of active ongoing research (2024–2026), with multiple recent works proposing constraints and possible detection channels (high-energy neutrinos, induced gravitational waves, gamma-ray signatures, LHAASO observations, binary mergers). No definitive resolution exists; the question remains open with partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Transitioning to Memory Burden: Detectable Small Primordial Black Holes as Dark Matter
status_evidence.snippet: In the memory burden scenario, evaporation is enormously suppressed, and sub-gram mass PBHs can survive to the present epoch.
status_evidence.claim: Memory-burdened PBHs can survive as relics; detection is being actively studied.

status_evidence.title: Micron-sized Extra Dimensions and Primordial Black Holes: Charges, Rotating, and Memory Burdened
status_evidence.snippet: Lifetime of near-extremal configurations is extended; extra-dimensional, charged, rotating, and memory-burdened scenarios analyzed.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional and near-extremal PBH stability is under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Constraining memory-burdened primordial black holes with graviton-photon conversion and binary mergers
status_evidence.snippet: Constraints from binary mergers and graviton-photon conversion on memory-burdened PBHs.
status_evidence.claim: Indirect detection via binary mergers of PBH relics is being explored but unresolved.
